title: Automatic port mapping
idea: Automatic port mapping lets Docker pick the host port for you, so many containers can use one container port without clashing.
points: `-P` publishes every `EXPOSE`d port on a random free host port.
`-p 3000` publishes only that container port on a random host port.
Docker picks an unused high host port, usually from the ephemeral range.
`docker port api-1` prints which host port Docker chose.

steps.caption: Run with `-P`. Docker reads `EXPOSE 3000` from the image and publishes that container port.
Docker binds a free host port, call it A, and forwards it to 3000. `docker port api-1` shows it.
A second `-P` run starts `api-2`. It also listens on 3000, so Docker gives it another host port, B.
Each host port reaches its own container. You picked no numbers, and nothing clashed.

code.caption: Two containers from one image, each on a host port Docker picked. The image has `EXPOSE 3000`.

walk.text: Same image twice with `-P`. Each container gets its own free host port.
List every mapping of `api-1`: container port, then host address and port.
Ask for one container port. Only the host side is printed.
`docker ps` shows mappings in its PORTS column; `--format` picks the columns.
`-p 3000` publishes only that port and lets Docker pick the host port.

pitfalls: `-P` skips ports the image does not expose. Add `EXPOSE` or use `-p`.
A new container can get a new port. Read it with `docker port`; never hard-code it.
Pick the host port yourself with `-p HOST:CONTAINER` when clients need a stable URL.

quiz.q: Both containers listen on 3000 inside. What happens?
quiz.code:
docker run -d -P --name api-1 bookstore-api
docker run -d -P --name api-2 bookstore-api
options: Both start, each on its own free host port
The second fails: host port 3000 is taken
Both start and share one host port
Only the first publishes a port
quiz.why: `-P` lets Docker pick an unused host port for each container, so two containers can share container port 3000.

takeaway: Let Docker pick the host port, then ask `docker port` where it landed.

starters: How do I find the port Docker assigned?
When should I use -P instead of -p?
